name: Engram
summary: Engram is building a learned memory layer that gives enterprise AI systems persistent organisational context.
overview: Engram emerged from stealth in June 2026 with $98 million in financing to build a memory layer for enterprise AI. It named Microsoft, Notion, and Harvey as early partners; the company did not announce a valuation.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Engram launched with the financing for its AI memory layer.

bull_case: Persistent organisational context is a core gap in enterprise AI, and a trusted memory layer can become deeply embedded across workflows.
bear_case: Data permissions, integration complexity, and competition from frontier-model providers and enterprise platforms could compress differentiation.
directory_notes: Public financial disclosure is limited, so this profile deliberately avoids representing a market estimate as a confirmed financing.

intelligence.description: A learned memory layer for enterprise AI systems and organisational context.
company: Engram is developing a memory layer intended to help enterprise AI systems understand an organisation rather than operate as a stateless general-purpose model.

Engram emerged from stealth with $98 million in financing from General Catalyst, Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia Capital, Factory, and others. Microsoft, Notion, and Harvey were named as early partners; no valuation was disclosed.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Memory and organisational context are likely to be key control points in enterprise AI stacks. Engram is a high-funded private effort to own that layer rather than leave it to application vendors or model providers.

changed.text: Engram emerged from stealth with $98M in financing and named early enterprise partners.

takeaways: The June 2026 financing is disclosed, but no valuation was announced.
Early partnerships are the first proof point for enterprise distribution.
Data access, trust, and platform competition are the primary risks.
